title: RECYCLING EVENT COMING
full_story:
B & H Recycling will be coming back to Flora on Saturday, May 16th.  B & H will be set up in the parking lot of the old Clay Medical Building, accepting items for recycling from 9 to 11 am.

Items accepted include stoves, washers, dryers, hot water heaters, refrigerators, freezers, dishwashers, air conditioners, central air units, heaters, electric motors, cars, car parts, tin, bicycles, lawn mowers, electric pumps, guttering, steel doors, aluminum windows, chop and band saws and anything that has an attached cord.  Items accepted for a $1 fee includes; fax machines, computers, keyboards, radios, VCR’s, CD & DVD players, mp3 players, game systems and stereos, cell phones and batteries, cameras and camcorders, grills, toasters, lamps, coffee pots, blenders, microwave ovens, printers, copiers, vacuums and dehumidifiers.  Items accepted for a $5 to $15 fee include small flat screen computer monitors, big screen tv’s, console TV’s with CRT glass and computer monitors.  B & H Recycling of West Liberty, IL, does not accept paint, tires, mattresses and box springs.

The recycling event is on Saturday, May 16th at the old Clay Medical Building from 9 to 11 am.

title: MARCH UNEMPLOYMENT DOWN IN MOST AREAS
full_story:
The Illinois Department of Labor Security released the March unemployment rates for the state.  The March unemployment rate in Clay County was 5.2% down from 5.8% in February.

The jobs report shows there were 5,896 people in the labor force, up 47 from February.  The total number of unemployed for the county was 309 down 33.

Around the area Effingham Counties March rate was 4.5% down from 4.9% in February.  Fayette County was at 6.1% down from 6.6% in February, and Marion County was at 5.4% down from 5.5% in February.  Richland and Wayne County’s rate was a little higher in March compared to February.  Richland Counties March rate was 4.8% compared to 4.7% in February and Wayne County was at 6.5% compared to Februarys 6.2%.

The highest unemployment rate in the state is in Edwards County where the rate is at 14.9% up 3.4% from February and up 10.7% from a year ago.  Monroe county had the lowest unemployment rate in the state at 3.2% down .1% from February.

The state unemployment rate for March was 5.2% down .03 from February and .9% higher than the national unemployment rate.

title: LOTHER ARRESTED
full_story:
Shane Lother, a South-Central High School choir and music teacher was arrested for grooming and traveling to meet a minor.  Lother, 38, was arrested at his home in Salem Friday afternoon.

South Central School Superintendent Kerry Herdes informed parents that the district had become aware of allegations of possible inappropriate relations between a minor and a high school teacher on February 26th.  Lother was immediately placed on administrative leave with local law enforcement and the Illinois Department of Children and Family Services being notified.

Evidence in the case was developed after forensic specialists with the Jefferson County Sheriff’s Department examined the cell phones of Lother and the alleged victim who is 15 years old.

Formal charges have not yet been filed, but are expected to be in place for Lother to make a first court appearance today.

title: FLORA CLEAN-UP DAYS
full_story:
The City of Flora will have town-wide clean-up days May 18th through the 22nd.

Accumulated, unwanted items at residences will be picked up at no extra charge on the residents normal trash day.  It is requested small or loose items should be bundled or bagged.  Carpet needs to be cut and tied so one person can handle it, broken glass items need to be bagged and marked for safety, multiple items such as brooms, mops, blinds, etc. need to be tied together, pool liners need to be cut down, and metal swing sets need to be broken down.  All mattresses and box springs must be wrapped in plastic, in order to be picked up.

For electronic items such as televisions and monitors, radios, tape recorders, computer hard drives, monitors, printers, cell phones, etc. residents are ask to please contact Secure Processors at 618-662-4823.

Republic Services, Flora’s solid waste hauler, will not accept any white goods such as stoves, dishwashers, washing machines, clothes dryers, etc., tires or vehicle/boat parts, paint, hazardous materials/waste, landscape waste, construction/remodeling/demolition materials, concrete/brick/asphalt, batteries, pressurized tanks, gas/oil/antifreeze, ammunition, or explosives.

Residents may deliver their properly decommissioned, no Freon or Oil, white goods to Public Works West lot at 200 Fairview Street.  Please follow the signs posted.  This will be a residential only pick up site.  The city will only be accepting white goods daily between the hours of 7:30 am to 3:30 pm.

Please keep weight in mind when grouping items, such as books and magazines, in a bag or trash container.

Residents with any further questions should call 618-662-4625 or email [email protected].

title: WILHOUR TRAVELING OFFICE HOURS
full_story:
State Representative Blaine Wilhour announced that his next Traveling Office Hours for constituents to meet with legislative staff to receive help with state programs is coming up.

On Wednesday legislative staff will be available at the Case-Halstead Library in Carlyle, from 9:00 am to 10:30 am, at the Centralia Regional Library from 11:00 am to 12:30 pm, and at the Bryan-Bennett Library in Salem from 2:00 pm to 3:30 pm.

Traveling Office Hours will also be held on Wednesday, May 20th at the Olney Public Library from 1 to 3 pm.

Representative Wilhour said “My staff will be available to meet with constituents about public policy issues and concerns as well as provide help with state programs.  I encourage everyone to sign up for my electronic news updates to learn about the activities of the General Assembly and encourage you to take advantage of the online technology to monitor legislative proceedings and file witness slips on legislation that you agree with or disagree with.”

Constituents may contact the district office at 618-665-4109 or online at RepWilhour.com to schedule an appointment to meet with the legislative staff.

title: 6K FOR WATER
full_story:
The 2026 6k for Water will be held on Saturday for walkers and runners from all over Southern Illinois.  This is the 10th year for Flora’s 6k for Water where people come together to raise money for clean water.  703 million people worldwide lack access to clean water.

Flora’s 6k for Water partners with the Christian Humanitarian Organization, World Vision.  In the past 9 years, Flora has raised over $60,000 for efforts that dig wells, build rain catchments, teach hygiene and more through World Vision.

6 kilometers or 3.7 miles, is the average distance that women and children all over the world walk daily for water.  As a result, children do not get the chance to go to school, they have the fear of being kidnapped and being trafficked.  Clean water within a village equals freedom from those things.  Nearly 800 children die each day from water-related illnesses.  You can help bring clean water to these communities.  World Vision reaches a new person with clean water every 10 seconds.

Sign up for the 6k at https://global6k.worldvision.org/teams/Flora2026

The race begins at 9 AM at the Flora First Christian Church.  No need to attend FCC to join.  This is a community event.

Each registration equals clean water for 1 person for the rest of their life.

The Flora 6k for Water will be held on Saturday at 9 AM at the Flora First Christian Church.

title: CARTERVILLE COACH ARRESTED
full_story:
The Williamson County Grand Jury indicted a former Carterville School District faculty member on nine counts of Aggravated Criminal Sexual Assault, according to the Williamson County Sheriff Jeff Diederich on Friday.

The sheriff said John Wakey was arrested in connection to allegations involving students from approximately more than 10 years ago.  Diederich said Wakey was a faculty member with the Carterville School District at the time the allegations took place.  According to court records, the charges date back to September 1st, 2013 to February 9th, 2015.

Diederich said there were a total of eight potential victims who were students at the time the alleged crimes took place.  Four of the victims have come forward about the allegations.  Authorities said Wakey was employed as a football coach during the alleged incidents from 2013 to 2015.  Wakey was taken into custody Thursday near Pontiac in Livingston County.

In March, the Carterville Community Unit School District 5 placed Wakey on administrative leave.  The district earlier stated they are continuing to cooperate with law enforcement and state agencies in the ongoing investigation into allegations of criminal sexual abuse and inappropriate conduct reported by a former student.  Superintendent Sarah Barnstable said in March a former student reported alleged criminal sexual abuse by a staff member to the Williamson County Sheriff’s Office.  The incidents were reported to have happened approximately 10 years ago during the student’s enrollment.

Barnstable said the district received credible information on February 20th and immediately acted by contacting the Illinois State Board of Education and placing the involved staff member on administrative leave.  The district also prohibited the employee from accessing school property.

The sheriff’s office also said Christopher C. Ballard was taken into custody on April 22nd.  The sheriff’s office says the arrest stems from allegations of sexual assault and abuse involving a female student that reportedly began when she was 16 years old.  The incidents are alleged to have occurred in 2016 and 2017.

Ballard faces two counts of aggravated criminal sexual assault, classified as Class X felonies under Illinois law, as well as two counts of aggravated criminal sexual abuse, classified as Class 2 felonies.

title: GRAZING CONFERENCE
full_story:
The 2026 Heart of America Grazing Conference will be held in Effingham on July 15th and 16th.

It will be the first time in several years Illinois has hosted the five-state rotating conference, according to the Illinois Grazing Lands Coalition.  A few highlights include the following; Farm tour at the operation of Curt Rincker, a Master Grazier Award recipient and past president of the Illinois Beef Association.  Keynote speaker Steve Campbell, known as the “cattle coach,” will discuss cattle genetics and grazing-based production.  Sessions will cover virtual fencing, cropland grazing, bale grazing and multi-species grazing, topics with growing interest among Illinois livestock producers.  And, the “Build a Regenerative Grazing System” competition for ages 14 through 22.

Registration is open at ilgrazinglands.org/events/heart-of-america-grazing-conference.
